2026-12-05.title: Saturday after the Sunday of the Visitation · Mar Saba; St Clement of Alexandria
readings: Never has anyone spoken like this
2026-12-05.alt: Mar Saba (St Sabbas), founder of the Great Lavra in the Judean desert (died 532), and Mar Clement of Alexandria, early Christian teacher (died around 215). The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo (Christmas), 1–24 December: prayer, fasting and almsgiving.
2026-12-05.verse: The police answered, “Never has anyone spoken like this!”
theo: Paul tells Timothy to have nothing to do with silly myths and to “train yourself in godliness”. Physical training has some value, but godliness is valuable in every way, “holding promise for both the present life and the life to come.” That is what a fast is: spiritual training. Mar Saba, whom the East remembers today, trained himself for decades in the desert and founded a monastery that still stands near Jerusalem.

The temple police were sent to arrest Jesus and came back empty-handed. Asked why, they could only say: “Never has anyone spoken like this!” The crowds argue whether he is the prophet or the Messiah; the leaders sneer that no prophet comes from Galilee. Only Nicodemus asks for a fair hearing. In this fast, let us give Jesus that fair hearing, listening to his word until, like the police, we are disarmed by it.

2026-12-05.prayer: Lord Jesus, no one has ever spoken as you speak. Train us in godliness during this fast, set our hope on the living God, and through the prayers of Mar Saba, let your word disarm our hearts. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we hear the words of the One who spoke like no one else, and receive him as the bread of eternal life.

2026-12-05.question: Have I given Jesus a fair hearing?

family.explain: Paul says we should train our souls like athletes train their bodies. Prayer and good habits make us strong in God.
family.intention: We pray for monks, nuns and all who live a life of prayer.
family.ask: Ask: “What good habit can we practise together during this fast?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, never has anyone spoken like you. As we gather, train us in godliness and give us courage to stand up for you. Amen.
share: Paul says godliness is valuable in every way (1 Timothy 4:8). What spiritual exercise do I need most?
The guards said: never has anyone spoken like this (John 7:46). Which words of Jesus have touched me most?
Like Nicodemus, where can I take a small step of courage for Christ?
pm.resp: Lord, train us in your ways.
interc: For monks and nuns, through the prayers of Mar Saba.
For teachers of the faith, through the prayers of St Clement of Alexandria.
For those divided about Jesus, that they may come to know him.
For the timid, that they may find courage to witness.
For our group, that we may grow in godliness.
pm.close: Lord God, Mar Saba and St Clement trained themselves in godliness. Help us to keep this fast as training of the soul, and to grow in faith step by step. Amen.

illus: A college student in Thiruvananthapuram decided during the Yaldo fast to wake up fifteen minutes early each day to read the Gospel. By the end of the fast she had read all of Luke. She said: “It was the first time I really heard Jesus speak.”

homily: Dear friends, today the Church remembers Mar Saba, the great monk of the Judean desert, and St Clement of Alexandria, an early teacher of the faith. Both trained themselves in godliness.

St Paul tells Timothy: train yourself in godliness, for while physical training is of some value, godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for both the present life and the life to come (1 Timothy 4:7–8). We train our bodies for health; how much more should we train our souls?

The fast is spiritual training. Like an athlete, we practise small disciplines: getting up for prayer, controlling our tongue, saying no to some food, saying yes to charity. These small exercises make the soul strong.

In the Gospel the people are divided about Jesus. Some say he is the prophet, others the Messiah. The temple police, sent to arrest him, return empty-handed and say: never has anyone spoken like this! (John 7:40–46). His words disarmed them.

Nicodemus, who had come to Jesus by night, now speaks up a little for him: our law does not judge people without first giving them a hearing (John 7:51). It is a small step of courage, but it is a beginning. Faith often grows by small steps.
This week, let us take one small step of courage for Christ, and one step of training in godliness. The Lord who spoke like no one else still speaks to us in the Gospel. Let us listen. Amen.
kids: Children, athletes train their bodies; Christians train their hearts with prayer and kindness. Train your heart today!

intro: Theme: “Never has anyone spoken like this.”
Training in godliness, listening to the Word.

sub: Joshua was to meditate on the law day and night.
Godliness holds promise for this life and the next.
q: This book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth; you shall meditate on it day and night,
for, while physical training is of some value, godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for both the present life and the life to come.
points.apply: Add five minutes of silent prayer to each day of the fast.

sub: The psalmist thirsts for the living God.
Paul toils because his hope is in him.
q: My soul thirsts for God, for the living God.
For to this end we toil and struggle, because we have our hope set on the living God, who is the Savior of all people, especially of those who believe.
points.apply: Offer your fasting as a prayer of hope.

sub: God promised a prophet who would speak his words.
The police say no one has spoken like Jesus.
q: I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their own people; I will put my words in the mouth of the prophet, who shall speak to them everything that I command.
The police answered, “Never has anyone spoken like this!”
points.apply: Read one Gospel chapter slowly today.

concl: The fast trains us; the Word disarms us.
